target.title: test(qa): migrate channel thread and DM isolation scenarios
target.body:
Closes #101111

## What Problem This Solves

Thread follow-up/isolation, reply override, subagent thread spawn, and direct-message session behavior were split across imperative Slack and Matrix scenario owners. That duplicated orchestration and made native relation evidence and cross-adapter parity harder to maintain.

## Why This Change Was Made

This migrates the parity-proven behavior family to six canonical YAML flows hosted by the shared scenario runner. Slack and Matrix adapters now expose the required stable normalized observations, including native thread/reply identifiers where available, and the replaced imperative owners and obsolete tests are removed rather than retained behind compatibility layers. Distinct Telegram and WhatsApp scenarios remain where their behavior is not exact parity.

## User Impact

No production channel behavior, routing, commands, restart/config surface, or infrastructure changes. QA ownership becomes canonical and shared across adapters, with less duplicated scenario code and clearer native relation evidence.

## Evidence

- Exact pushed head: `42470aa9c3830e59d1f69d87b8b656f9f64932b6`.
- Focused Testbox proof: 9 files / 208 tests passed across QA Lab and Matrix; rebased lint plus 205 focused tests passed; Matrix env-bridge repair lint plus 105 tests passed; Slack facade repair prod `tsgo`, bundled lint, and 41 tests passed.
- qa-channel `thread-follow-up` and `thread-isolation` passed: `.artifacts/qa-e2e/suite-mr9jlf2y-a24d200a/qa-suite-report.md`.
- Matrix Crabline `thread-follow-up` and `thread-isolation` passed with native relation evidence: `.artifacts/qa-e2e/suite-mr9jlsag-934ec4cd/qa-suite-report.md`.
- Matrix live thread reply override passed.
- Matrix live shared-DM passed: `.artifacts/qa-e2e/suite-mr9ijndt-1b96c71f/qa-suite-report.md`.
- Matrix live per-room DM passed: `.artifacts/qa-e2e/suite-mr9ikpna-ab6f4a58/qa-suite-report.md`.
- Telegram Crabline relation proof is inapplicable because its fake API does not echo `message_thread_id`; Matrix is the applicable bridge selected by the canonical thread flows.
- QA Smoke on `b47b2c9db1f2cc092d17b63c0492a27b1858ffd5` timed out only in `thread-follow-up` and `thread-isolation` because the default Telegram Crabline fake transport cannot preserve native topic relation. The scenarios now declare `execution.channel: matrix`, preserving qa-channel execution while selecting the proven native relation bridge for Crabline and current explicit-lane validation.
- Post-rebase focused proof on current main: `git diff --check` passed and scenario catalog plus suite-planning tests passed 61/61 using the narrow local fallback because Testbox capacity was explicitly quiesced.
- Current correction proof: scenario catalog and suite-planning tests pass 61/61; fresh Codex autoreview completed clean with no accepted/actionable findings (confidence 0.86).
- QA Smoke CI is intentionally disabled upstream by #101185 / `6bffda416614780b1b129891615b4a43cadb4080` after #101184 reverted the selector experiment. This PR does not modify selector or CI workflow files.
- ClawSweeper finding resolved: historical commit `c3308b91955` made Matrix subagent thread spawn explicit-only; the canonical `subagent-thread-spawn` YAML remains explicitly selectable, but is removed from the default Matrix adapter set until live child-completion proof is stable. Focused Testbox proof passed Matrix CLI 4/4 and scenario catalog 36/36; four-file `oxfmt` check passed; fresh Codex autoreview was clean at 0.88.
- Current ClawSweeper finding resolved: Matrix account-relative scenario patches use the canonical `$selectedAccount` key, resolved by the shared suite runner from `adapterOptions.sutAccountId` before merge. Focused proof covers `--scenario thread-reply-override --sut-account matrix-alt`, the real YAML patch resolves under `accounts.matrix-alt`, and all three affected Matrix patches use the same contract. Rebased Testbox run 28832185349 passed scoped `oxfmt` plus 69 focused tests; fresh exact-commit Codex autoreview was clean at 0.84.
- Known bounded gap: Matrix emitted the native subagent `session active` thread intro immediately on both attempts, but the child completion did not arrive before either 360-second hard timeout.
- AI-assisted implementation; no transcript attached.
